audits.dominantPattern: Pattern 5 preamble/non-reaction negation and emphatic restatement of already-established facts
clusterPages: Cyndia briefing, lines 237-257: 4 kills (L237, L247, L251, L257) -> severe cluster
clusterWarnings: Non-reaction beat shape repeats across scenes: 'He didn't smile.' (L151), 'She didn't raise her voice.' (L219), 'Cyndia didn't hesitate over it' (L251)
Three-hypothesis-then-'None of' shape repeats: L211 (kept, first instance) and L257 (killed)

findings.text: Nobody was arguing about trolls now.
findings.deletionTest: Paragraph reads: 'Behind her the patrol had come up, bunching along the trail. So much for Cyndia never wanting anything from her.' Survives; the negation only defines the patrol's state by what it stopped doing.
findings.reason: Defines the patrol's mood by the absence of a prior action; sits beside a second negation callback ('never wanting anything') in the same paragraph. No binary diagnostic, spatial precision, or hard constraint.
findings.suggestedFix: Every one of them was listening.

findings.text: He didn't smile.
findings.deletionTest: '"Someone has to tell them."' Survives; the line itself carries his refusal to banter.
findings.reason: Pattern 5: defines his reaction by the reaction he did not have. Same non-reaction shape recurs at L219 and L251.
findings.suggestedFix: He let the joke go by.

findings.text: with Dalaran, both was never out of the question.
findings.deletionTest: No positive half exists; the clause states possibility by negating impossibility.
findings.reason: Double-negative litotes standing in for a plain positive ('could be both'); no keep condition applies. (Note for slophunter: L209 repeats the same 'both' joke - 'With the Kirin Tor it was always worth considering both.' Repetition is outside pass A scope, but the positive fix below avoids a third phrasing of 'always'.)
findings.suggestedFix: with Dalaran, it could easily be both.

findings.text: What a right one looked like, she could not have said. Still less a wrong one.
findings.deletionTest: Paragraph keeps 'She could not read a leyline.' two sentences later, which states the same capability boundary. Survives and tightens.
findings.reason: Adversarial self-check 1: deleting the pair loses no concrete fact; the hard constraint is carried by 'She could not read a leyline.' The pair is a negation echo in a paragraph already dense with negations (L207-213).

findings.text: She didn't raise her voice.
findings.deletionTest: '"Cyndia." Everyone in the yard had already turned...' Survives; the reason clause already shows she needed no volume.
findings.reason: Pattern 5: defines her delivery by the action she did not take. Repeats the non-reaction shape of L151.

findings.text: Not one ranger on the wall had seen her.
findings.deletionTest: Paragraph ends '...laid her hands on it six times. "Go on."' Survives; the unseen crossing is already established at L117 ('Nobody saw her cross'), L155 ('without a single ranger seeing her'), and L231 ('Nobody saw her before dawn').
findings.reason: Fourth negation-framed statement of the same fact; 'Not one' is emphasis, not information. Part of the L237-257 severe cluster.

findings.text: He says every one reads like the trouble's inside it, not on the face.
findings.deletionTest: 'He says every one reads like the trouble's inside it.' Survives; 'inside' already excludes the face, and the preceding sentences say 'only there's not a mark on it' and 'Every one looks as it has for a hundred years.'
findings.reason: Pattern 1 tail: the negative half restates a distinction the same speech has already made twice. The earlier 'only there's not a mark on it' is kept as the physical-precision instance. Part of the L237-257 severe cluster.
findings.suggestedFix: He says every one reads like the trouble's inside it.

findings.text: Cyndia didn't hesitate over it, which was the thing Sylvanas had always valued in her.
findings.deletionTest: No positive half; the trait Sylvanas values is defined only by the hesitation that did not happen.
findings.reason: Defines Cyndia's delivery by negation; third non-reaction beat in the chapter (with L151, L219). Part of the L237-257 severe cluster.
findings.suggestedFix: Cyndia said it straight out, which was the thing Sylvanas had always valued in her.

findings.text: None of them was a spy. She was nearly certain none of them was an envoy.
findings.deletionTest: 'Sylvanas could make three women out of that: one arrogant, one frightened, and one who'd simply been right in the wrong country.' Survives; the three positive readings already displace spy and envoy, and L207-211 ran the full elimination on the ride.
findings.reason: Cluster rule: repeats the L211 'three options, then None of' shape in a new scene, chaining two negations to re-close a question the chapter already closed. Part of the L237-257 severe cluster.

findings.text: She had expected violet. She hadn't known she was expecting it until it wasn't there: silk,
findings.deletionTest: 'She had expected violet: silk, and rings on soft fingers, and the smooth, well-fed face of someone who had spent her life in rooms where people listened.' Survives and improves.
findings.reason: The middle sentence is a double-negation flourish ('hadn't known... until it wasn't there') sitting between the expectation and its catalog. 'This one hadn't.' at paragraph end is kept as the binary diagnostic.

audits.dominantPattern: Pattern 8 body-part / stride subjects carrying the character's volition, plus static landscape given body-behavior verbs (P5/P6 sweep)
clusterFlags: Storeroom close, lines 327-333: 2 body-part kills (L327 hands shifted, L333 mouth arguing)
audits.secondSweepP5P6: Re-read every sentence for inanimate/abstract/body-part subjects. Found: static landscape with body-behavior or motion verbs (L193 trees folded, L197 boulders shouldering); receiver noun with the real keeper omitted (L55 apple lived); body-part/stride subjects (L123, L267, L327, L333). Rule applied consistently: a genuinely physical agent making literal contact or motion (sweat crept, axe kissed, wind pushed, cold air met, cold mineral bite pouring down) is KEEP under condition 3; a static object given motion or human-body behavior is KILL. No abstract-state-settling-into-body cases (L13 'old ache settled back into the joint' is a literal physical pain). No consecutive-sentence metaphor chains on one inanimate subject.

findings.text: hunting the dried apple that usually lived in that cuff
findings.subject: the dried apple
findings.realAgent: Sylvanas, who keeps an apple in her cuff for the mare
findings.reason: Pattern 10: the keeper is omitted and the apple gets the habitation verb; putting Sylvanas back in subject position keeps the same meaning.
findings.suggestedFix: hunting the dried apple she usually kept in that cuff

findings.text: Her mother's hand was closing on the back of her collar—*not those, never those*.
findings.subject: her mother's hand
findings.reason: Pattern 8: the hand performs the mother's deliberate grab; 'Her mother caught her by the collar' means the same thing. Not a reflex.
findings.suggestedFix: Her mother caught her by the back of the collar—*not those, never those*.

findings.text: until the trees folded over the sound
findings.subject: the trees
findings.realAgent: distance and foliage muffling the receding patrol
findings.reason: Second-sweep catch: static trees given a folding action; nothing in the scene moves except the patrol.
findings.suggestedFix: until the sound faded out among the trees

findings.text: grey boulders shouldering up out of the thin soil
findings.subject: grey boulders
findings.realAgent: none; the boulders protrude from the soil
findings.reason: Second-sweep catch: static rock given a human-body pushing verb.
findings.suggestedFix: grey boulders jutting up out of the thin soil

findings.text: Three strides took her to the barred door.
findings.subject: three strides
findings.reason: Pattern 8 cousin of the calibration line 'Her feet carried her across the room'; the strides carry her instead of her walking.
findings.suggestedFix: She crossed to the barred door in three strides.

findings.text: chain clinked faintly as the mage's hands shifted in her lap, then went quiet
findings.subject: the mage's hands
findings.reason: Pattern 8: the sentence is about the chain sound, so the involuntary-movement exception does not apply; 'the mage moved her hands' means the same thing.
findings.suggestedFix: chain clinked faintly as the mage moved her hands in her lap, then went quiet

findings.text: the chapped mouth that had been arguing all day and was shut now
findings.subject: the chapped mouth
findings.reason: Pattern 8: arguing is deliberate speech belonging to the mage; the mouth takes her volition. Clusters with A-IS-6 on the closing page.
findings.suggestedFix: the chapped mouth, shut now after a day of arguing
